content: Courage is the most important of all the virtues because without courage, you can't practice any other virtue consistently.
author: Maya Angelou
sourceWork: Wouldn't Take Nothing for My Journey Now (1993)
story:
There is a sharp, grounded clarity in this observation. Holding onto anger is like clutching a glowing coal with the intent of throwing it at someone else—you are the one who gets burned. Retaliation only ties you tighter to the person who harmed you.

In Maya Angelou's view, genuine strength is not an abstract theory—it is a lived, daily practice. Forgiveness and composure are not signs of weakness or giving someone a pass. They are acts of fierce self-preservation, cutting the emotional chain that allows another person's bad behavior to ruin your peace of mind.
reflectionPrompt: Where does your life require a quiet act of courage from you before this week ends?

practicalInsight: When someone triggers your temper today, take three slow breaths before responding. Do not give away your power for the sake of a quick comeback.
